title: Protocol for density gradient neutrophil isolation and flow cytometry-based characterization from human peripheral blood
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for density gradient neutrophil isolation and flow cytometry-based characterization from human peripheral blood

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedure for isolating neutrophils from human peripheral blood using a two-layer Percoll density gradient, followed by their characterization via flow cytometry. The process involves preparing specific reagent solutions, performing the density gradient centrifugation to separate cell populations, washing and counting isolated neutrophils, staining cells with fluorophore-conjugated antibodies, and finally acquiring data on a flow cytometer using appropriate controls for compensation and voltage setting.

### Materials/Reagents

Percoll (for 62% and 75% gradient solutions), 10× PBS, Ultra-pure H2O, Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) for 10% BSA buffer, RPMI 1640 medium (serum-free, without antibiotics), 1× HBSS, 1M HEPES, Neutrophil buffer (composed of 1× HBSS, 5 mM HEPES, and 0.2% BSA), FACS buffer, Fc Block, Fluorophore-conjugated antibodies (titrated), Compensation beads, Unstained and single-stained controls for each fluorophore used in the panel.

### Equipment

Sterile serological pipettes, sterile transfer pipettes or micropipettes, 50 mL conical tubes, disposable hemocytometer, microscope, 96-well U-bottom plates, round-bottom polystyrene tubes, multichannel micropipette, centrifuge (capable of zero acceleration/deceleration settings), flow cytometer.

### Safety & Sterility

All procedures must be performed in a biosafety cabinet. All reagents should be brought to room temperature (20-25°C) before use during the isolation phase. Care must be taken to maintain sterility throughout the process.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare the 62% Percoll gradient solution by mixing 31 mL of 62% Percoll, 5 mL of 10× PBS, and 14 mL of Ultra-pure H2O to achieve a total volume of 50 mL. Store the solution at 4°C and use within 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare the 75% Percoll gradient solution by mixing 37.5 mL of 75% Percoll, 5 mL of 10× PBS, and 7.5 mL of Ultra-pure H2O to achieve a total volume of 50 mL. Store the solution at 4°C and use within 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. %10 BSA Reagent Final concentration Amount BSA 10 mg/mL (10%) 10 g 1× PBS N/A 100 mL **Total** **N/A** **100 mL** Store at 4°C, use within 6 months [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare the Neutrophil buffer by mixing 500 mL of 1× HBSS, 2.5 mL of 1M HEPES (final concentration 5 mM), and 10 mL of 10% BSA buffer (final concentration 0.2%) to achieve a total volume of 512.5 mL. Store the solution at 4°C and use within 6 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->

## Neutrophil Isolation

### 1-1.5 h

> **Operational constraint:** Ensure all reagents are brought to room temperature (20-25°C). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Perform all procedures in a biosafety cabinet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
1. Add 10 mL of 75% Percoll into a 50 mL conical tube using a sterile serological pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
2. Carefully overlay 10 mL of 62% Percoll on top of the 75% Percoll layer using a sterile serological pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
3. Dilute 10 mL of fresh blood 1:1 with 10 mL of serum-free RPMI 1640 without antibiotics. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
4. Carefully overlay 20 mL of the diluted blood on top of the 62% Percoll layer using a sterile serological pipette in a dropwise manner, bringing the total volume to 40 mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Set the centrifuge acceleration and deceleration to zero before proceeding with centrifugation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
5. Centrifuge the 50 mL conical tubes at 200 × g for 25 minutes, followed by centrifugation at 400 × g for 15 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
6. Carefully remove the tubes from the centrifuge without disrupting the gradient layers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
7. Use sterile transfer pipettes or micropipettes to collect the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) located on top of the 62% Percoll layer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
8. Use sterile transfer pipettes or micropipettes to collect the neutrophils positioned between the 75% and 62% Percoll layers, and transfer these cells to a new 50 mL conical tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note that PBMCs are positioned on top of the 62% Percoll layer, while red blood cells (RBCs) form a pellet underneath the 75% Percoll layer; ensure careful collection of neutrophils without disrupting the RBC layer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
9. Add RPMI 1640 to the neutrophil-containing tube up to a volume of 50 mL, then wash the neutrophils by centrifuging at 300 × g for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
10. Remove the supernatant completely and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of neutrophil buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
11. Add 10 μL of the cell suspension to a disposable hemocytometer and count the cell number under a microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Critical Step: Ensure careful overlay of the 62% Percoll on top of the 75% Percoll layer, and subsequent careful overlay of diluted blood on top of the 62% Percoll layer to obtain good separation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->

## Neutrophil Staining for Flow Cytometry

### 1-2 h

1. Add 0.5-1 × 10^6 neutrophils in 100 μL of neutrophil buffer per well into the appropriate wells of a 96-well U-bottom plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 200 μL of FACS buffer per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
5. Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of FACS buffer containing Fc Block (diluted 1:100 in FACS buffer) for 20 minutes on ice or at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
6. Centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->
7. Perform staining according to the following steps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S07 -->
8. Resuspend the unstained control in 100 μL of FACS buffer per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S08 -->
9. Stain the cells with the appropriate volume of antibodies based on titration results. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S09 -->
10. Prepare FMO (Fluorescence Minus One) controls by staining the cells with all antibodies except one. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S10 -->
11. Mix each well by pipetting up and down using a multichannel micropipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S11 -->
12. Wrap the plate in foil to protect from light and incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S12 -->
13. Following incubation, centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C, discard the supernatant, and wash cells with 200 μL of FACS buffer per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S13 -->
14. Centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S14 -->
15. Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 200 μL of FACS buffer per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S15 -->

## Acquisition on Flow Cytometer

### 1-2 h

1. Prepare unstained and single-stained controls for every fluorophore used in the panel to correct for fluorescence spillover and set appropriate voltages for each channel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. Add 100 μL of FACS buffer per well in a 96-well U-bottom plate or per tube in round-bottom polystyrene tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Add one drop of compensation beads to each well containing FACS buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Vortex the beads for 1 minute prior to use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
5. Add 1 μL of the antibody to respective wells, excluding the unstained control. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
6. Wrap the plate in foil to protect from light and incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
7. Following incubation, centrifuge the plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->
8. Discard the supernatant and resuspend beads in 200 μL of FACS buffer per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S08 -->
9. Run the unstained and single-stained beads to set appropriate photomultiplier tube (PMT) voltages and the compensation matrix, followed by the acquisition of samples. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S10 -->
